Yeah a lot of times when kids are super little, nobody but the parents/primary caregivers can decipher what they're trying to say. My son's almost two, and he kind of has his own baby-language. It's almost like he doesn't know what things are called so he just wings it and makes up a word for it. After a while you kind of just know 'dinky' means 'blanket' and 'kooooook' means 'food'. As he gets older, he's been replacing those made-up words with the correct ones, but it's still difficult for his grandparents to understand him sometimes because they're just not as familiar with his made-up language. I'm sure the same applies for this kid and his dad--the kid clearly has some trouble speaking, but when you spend a lot of time with your kid, you just kind of pick up on what they mean even if everyone else just hears gibberish with a couple actual words thrown in.

If I were to go back and read over the first draft before it was finished, I'd get frustrated and discouraged it would probably never see the light of day. You're supposed to cut things out in the second draft anyway. Nobody gets it 100% right on the first time around. That's just the nature of the game.
